brief: Stronger US/Eurozone flash PMIs plus UN rhetoric (Iran deal further off, no Russia-sanctions consensus) drove bond yields sharply higher because the market had been underpricing terminal Fed funds; the 5Y yield broke 5% for the first time since 2007 after a 3.20bp-tail auction with weak demand. Composite PMI hit 58.4, a five-year high, consistent with roughly 5% annualized growth, but input-cost inflation posted its largest monthly rise since 2020, raising hike risk (the market now sees the next Fed hike in October; Barr says more hikes are likely needed). Because SPX earnings track nominal, not real, GDP, JPM argues the equity bull market can persist, though bond vol, not the yield level, is the bigger equity risk. Brent broke back above $100 on Iranian escalatory rhetoric and unresolved Hormuz/Bab al-Mandab tensions; Pezeshkian said Iran's demands (MoU return, end to kinetic hostilities, unfrozen funds) are unchanged. JPM stays Tactically Cautious/Neutral, running +Tech vs -RTY (dollar- or market-neutral), bullish only if oil/yields fall, bearish if the consumer breaks or AI capex is cut. Futures positioning stays broadly cautious despite the equity rebound.
